dataset/block-cell.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 value cells. A block in a cell on a message column. MUST be
# accepted: a cell means what `nested_field = { name = "inner" value = 99 }`
# means in a body. Rejected before v1.13, when cells were scalar-only.

dataset/block-on-scalar.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 value cells. A block in a cell on a scalar column. MUST be
# rejected, binding the row: the cell means `int32_field = { value = 1 }`,
# and a block on a scalar field is an error in a body too.

dataset/cell-framing.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 value cells. Row framing. MUST be accepted: two rows. A ")" or ","
# inside a string, a triple-quoted string or a comment within a block cell
# neither ends the row nor splits the cell. A streaming reader finds the
# row by matching parentheses outside strings and comments, so it MUST
# yield the same two rows as a materializing parse.

dataset/dotted-bad-header-empty-row.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths. Row type dataset.v1.Event in paths.proto. MUST be
# rejected at the header: picks is a repeated field. The row's cells are
# all empty, and the header rules apply to it all the same, since they
# do not depend on what a row holds.

dataset/dotted-bad-header-no-rows.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths. Row type dataset.v1.Event in paths.proto. MUST be
# accepted: picks is a repeated field, so the header breaks a rule that
# needs the row type, but those rules are checked when a row binds, and
# this table has no rows. Compare dotted-bad-header-empty-row, which has
# one row of empty cells and is rejected.

dataset/dotted-column.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths. A column may be a dotted path into a sub-message.
# MUST be accepted. The row binds as
#   string_field = "row-1" nested_field { name = "inner" }
# Before v1.13 a dotted column was rejected.

dataset/dotted-grouping.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths, the grouping rule. Row type dataset.v1.Event in
# paths.proto. MUST be accepted. A row binds as the body that groups its
# non-empty cells by path prefix, one block per prefix, wherever the
# columns sit in the header:
#
#   r1: id "r1" desc { energy 0.5 tempo { min_bpm 60 max_bpm 120 } tags ["x"] } plain 1
#   r2: id "r2" desc { energy 0.25 } plain 2       (every desc.tempo.* cell
#       is empty, so tempo is absent)
#   r3: id "r3" plain 3                            (every desc.* cell is
#       empty, so desc is absent)
#   r4: id "r4" desc { tempo { max_bpm 9 } } plain 4

dataset/dotted-into-any.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths. Row type dataset.v1.Event in paths.proto. MUST be
# accepted: payload is a google.protobuf.Any, and a path into it names
# the Any's own fields, as a block with no type entry does (§3.16). The
# row binds as
#   id = "x" payload { type_url = "type.googleapis.com/dataset.v1.Pick" value = b"CgF4" }

dataset/dotted-into-bignum.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths. Row type dataset.v1.Event in paths.proto. MUST be
# rejected at the header: big is a pxf.BigInt, which is written as a
# literal.

dataset/dotted-into-duration.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths. Row type dataset.v1.Event in paths.proto. MUST be
# rejected at the header: dur is a google.protobuf.Duration, which is
# written as a literal.

dataset/dotted-into-secret.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths. Row type dataset.v1.Event in paths.proto. MUST be
# accepted: pw is a pxf.Secret, which is not on the list of types written
# as a literal, because its block form is one people write. The row binds
# as
#   id = "x" pw { value = "s3cret" hint = "db password" }

dataset/dotted-into-timestamp.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths. Row type dataset.v1.Event in paths.proto. MUST be
# rejected at the header: ts is a google.protobuf.Timestamp, which is
# written as a literal, so a path into its encoding is not a column.

dataset/dotted-into-wrapper.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths. Row type dataset.v1.Event in paths.proto. MUST be
# rejected at the header: wrap is a google.protobuf.Int32Value, which is
# written as a literal.

dataset/dotted-null-leaf.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths. Row type dataset.v1.Event in paths.proto. MUST be
# accepted. null in a dotted cell applies to the leaf, as
#   desc { label = null }
# does in a body: label (a wrapper) is unset, and desc is present.

dataset/dotted-oneof-two-members.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths. Row type dataset.v1.Event in paths.proto. MUST be
# rejected: the row fills two members of the oneof `choice`, which the
# body  a { name = "x" } b { name = "y" }  would be rejected for.

dataset/dotted-oneof.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths. Row type dataset.v1.Event in paths.proto. MUST be
# accepted. Columns may reach different members of the oneof `choice`,
# and two columns may fill the same member: they share one block, so the
# member is set once.
#
#   row 1: a { name "x" n 1 }
#   row 2: b { name "y" }

dataset/dotted-required-missing.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths. Row type dataset.v1.Event in paths.proto, whose
# Req.n is (pxf.required). MUST be rejected: req.d makes req present, and
# req.n is empty, as  req { d = "x" }  is rejected in a body.

dataset/dotted-required.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths. Row type dataset.v1.Event in paths.proto, whose
# Req.n is (pxf.required) and Req.d has (pxf.default) "dflt". MUST be
# accepted. Both apply under a present parent only, as in a body:
#
#   "absent": every req.* cell is empty, so req is absent, and req.n is
#             not required
#   "set":    req { n 5 }, and req.d takes its default "dflt"

dataset/dotted-through-map.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths. Row type dataset.v1.Event in paths.proto. MUST be
# rejected at the header: by_name is a map field, and a path has no key.

dataset/dotted-through-repeated.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths. Row type dataset.v1.Event in paths.proto. MUST be
# rejected at the header: picks is a repeated field, and a path has no
# index. A value cell on picks is the way to write it.

dataset/dotted-through-scalar.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths. Row type dataset.v1.Event in paths.proto. MUST be
# rejected at the header: plain is an int32, not a message field, so a
# path cannot go through it.

dataset/dotted-unknown-segment.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths. Row type dataset.v1.Event in paths.proto. MUST be
# rejected at the header: dataset.v1.Desc has no field nope.

dataset/dotted-with-value-cells.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 column paths beside value cells. Row type dataset.v1.Event in
# paths.proto. MUST be accepted. A dotted column may hold a list or a
# block, and plain columns may hold value cells next to it:
#
#   id "m" desc { energy 0.5 tempo { min_bpm 60 } tags ["a", "b"] }
#          picks [{ name "p" }]

dataset/empty-rows.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 zero-row table. Valid — a header with no rows denotes an empty
# dataset. MUST be accepted.

dataset/list-cell.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 value cells. A list in a cell on a repeated column. MUST be
# accepted: a cell means what `repeated_string = ["alpha", "beta"]` means
# in a body. Rejected before v1.13, when cells were scalar-only.

dataset/nested-cells.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 value cells. MUST be accepted. Each row binds to the message its
# body would: a non-empty cell in column c means `c = <value>`.
#
#   row-1: nested_field {name "n1" value 1}; repeated_string [a, b];
#          repeated_nested [{x}, {y 2}]; string_map {k: v}; int32_field 1
#   row-2: nested_field present and empty ({}); repeated_string empty ([]);
#          repeated_nested and string_map absent (empty cells); int32_field 2
#   row-3: every nested column absent; int32_field 3
#   row-4: nested_field null (present-but-null, as `nested_field = null`
#          is in a body); the other nested columns absent; int32_field 4

dataset/null-on-optional-cell.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 + § Booleans, Null, and Identifier Values (#339). Row type
# dataset.v1.Event in paths.proto. MUST be accepted: a cell applies the
# singular-field null rules, and opt is an optional scalar, so the null
# leaves it unset and present-but-null.

dataset/null-on-scalar-cell.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 + § Booleans, Null, and Identifier Values (#339). Row type
# test.v1.AllTypes. MUST be rejected: a cell applies the singular-field
# null rules, and int32_field is a plain scalar.

dataset/rows-end-at-directive.pxf.format:
# §3.4.4 appending. Two datasets in one document. The first one's rows end
# at the second "@dataset" directive, which is a legitimate end of the
# sequence. MUST be accepted: two datasets, two rows and one row.

duplicates/err-null-then-value.pxf.format:
@type dup.v1.Holder

# Reject: null is a binding, so a value after it binds the field a second time.
w = null
w = 3

duplicates/err-oneof-scalar-twice.pxf.format:
@type dup.v1.Holder

# Reject: a scalar oneof member bound twice.
ks = "a"
ks = "b"

duplicates/err-optional-twice.pxf.format:
@type dup.v1.Holder

# Reject: a proto3 optional scalar bound twice.
o = 1
o = 2

duplicates/err-scalar-same-value.pxf.format:
@type dup.v1.Holder

# Reject: a singular scalar bound twice, even to the same value.
s = "a"
s = "a"

duplicates/err-scalar-twice.pxf.format:
@type dup.v1.Holder

# Reject: a singular scalar bound twice. The second binding is the error; it does not replace the first.
s = "a"
s = "b"

duplicates/err-wrapper-twice.pxf.format:
@type dup.v1.Holder

# Reject: a wrapper is a singular field; binding it twice is rejected.
w = 1
w = 2

duration/negative-fractional.pxf.format:
@type duration.v1.Holder

# A fractional segment under a leading "-" yields seconds and nanos of the
# same sign, as google.protobuf.Duration requires: seconds = -1,
# nanos = -500000000.
d = -1.5s

duration/negative-multi-segment.pxf.format:
@type duration.v1.Holder

# The sign applies to the whole literal, not to its first segment:
# -1h30m is minus ninety minutes, seconds = -5400.
d = -1h30m

duration/negative-seconds.pxf.format:
@type duration.v1.Holder

# A negative Duration is written with one leading "-" before the first
# segment. Binds to seconds = -30, nanos = 0.
d = -30s

map-keys/fmt-keyword-keys.pxf.marshal:
by_label = {
  "123": "quoted integer"
  "false": "quoted keyword"
  "null": "quoted keyword"
  "true": "quoted keyword"
  bare: "bare identifier"
  plain: "quoted identifier-safe key"
}

nulls/default-optional.pxf.format:
@type nulls.v1.Defaulted

# Accept: null on an optional scalar with a (pxf.default). The default
# applies only to an absent field: d stays unset, not 5, and is
# present-but-null.
d = null

nulls/editions-explicit.pxf.format:
@type nulls.ed.v1.Ed

# Accept: in an editions file, a scalar with EXPLICIT presence (the 2023
# default) may hold null; it is left unset and present-but-null.
explicit_scalar = null

nulls/err-editions-implicit.pxf.format:
@type nulls.ed.v1.Ed

# Reject: an editions scalar with IMPLICIT presence has no unset state, so
# null would read back as zero.
implicit_scalar = null

nulls/err-map.pxf.format:
@type nulls.v1.Holder

# Reject: null on a map field. A map is not nullable; write {} for an
# empty one.
m = null

nulls/err-proto2-required.pxf.format:
@type nulls.v1.Strict

# Reject: null on a proto2 required field (#379). It has explicit
# presence, but leaving it unset would make the message invalid in
# binary, so the null is an error.
r = null

nulls/err-repeated.pxf.format:
@type nulls.v1.Holder

# Reject: null on a repeated field. A list is not nullable; write []
# for an empty one.
l = null

nulls/err-scalar.pxf.format:
@type nulls.v1.Holder

# Reject: null on a plain proto3 scalar field. It has no unset state, so
# null would read back as 0. Declare it optional, or as its wrapper type,
# to make it nullable.
n = null

nulls/oneof-message.pxf.format:
@type nulls.v1.Holder

# Accept: null on a message member of a oneof clears it: the oneof k is
# unset.
km = null

nulls/oneof-scalar.pxf.format:
@type nulls.v1.Holder

# Accept: null on a scalar member of a oneof. A member has explicit
# presence: the oneof k is unset, and ks is present-but-null.
ks = null

nulls/optional-scalar.pxf.format:
@type nulls.v1.Holder

# Accept: null on an optional scalar field. Explicit presence gives the
# field an unset state: o is unset, and present-but-null.
o = null

nulls/proto2-scalar.pxf.format:
@type nulls.v1.Legacy

# Accept: null on a proto2 optional scalar. It has explicit presence: p
# is unset, and present-but-null.
p = null

nulls/required-optional.pxf.format:
@type nulls.v1.Required

# Accept: null on an optional scalar marked (pxf.required). A null field
# is present for that check: r is unset, and present-but-null.
r = null

nulls/wrapper.pxf.format:
@type nulls.v1.Holder

# Accept: null on a wrapper field. The wrapper makes the scalar
# nullable: w is unset, and present-but-null.
w = null

repeated/err-scalar-entries.pxf.format:
@type test.v1.AllTypes

# Entries and Keys: a repeated field bound to a scalar. MUST be rejected —
# a repeated field is written with a list value: repeated_string = ["a", "b"].
repeated_string = "a"
repeated_string = "b"

strings/escaped-newline.pxf.format:
@type strings.v1.Holder

# Accept: the escape \n is how a simple string holds a line break.
# Binds s to "x", LF, "y".
s = "x\ny"

strings/newline-after-string.pxf.format:
@type strings.v1.Holder

# Accept: a newline after a closed string ends the entry, not the string.
# Binds s to "x" and t to "y".
s = "x"
t = "y"

strings/triple-quoted.pxf.format:
@type strings.v1.Holder

# Accept: a triple-quoted string may span lines. Binds s to "x", LF, "y"
# (the leading LF after the opening quotes and the common indent are
# stripped).
s = "x\ny"
